transcript: The sledgehammer shattering the glass of the pinball machine, but this isn't some crazy vandal This is New York's mayor Fiorello LaGuardia Yep The guy the airport's named after and he's doing this in front of newspaper cameras as part of his war on pinball LaGuardia came to Office in 1934 promising to fight organized crime which after the repeal of prohibition had moved into slot machines But when LaGuardia had stamped them out he switched to pinball, but this wasn't pinball like we know it today though There were no flippers just a cue to shoot the ball pockets and bouncers and they also distributed prizes, from gum to cigars to money, and while businesses used these machines to get people through the door, they were also a cash business great for money laundering. So in 1942, LaGuardia convinced the federal government that pinball was a waste of war resources. He had the game outlawed and conducted prohibition-style raids on the machines, stamping them out. And pinball would remain illegal in New York until 1976, when the addition of flippers convinced city authorities that this was a game of skill, not luck.
